papers.key_result: Calibration-leverage tradeoff in win-probability models: sharpens the diagnostic for when GSE's calibrated probabilities lose leverage against market lines. Calibration without leverage is inert — a calibrated model that never moves off the market price has zero betting value. Adaptation: jointly track calibration error and leverage (probability movement vs bookmaker) as a model-health pair.
papers.title: The calibration-leverage tradeoff in win-probability models

papers.key_result: Favorite-longshot bias documented in Polymarket prediction markets: longshots overpriced, favorites underpriced relative to realized outcomes — a structural, exploitable mispricing. Adaptation: build a Polymarket price-vs-model disagreement scanner for GSE; overweight value on favorites where the bias is largest, and treat longshot market prices as inflated.
papers.title: Favorite-longshot bias in prediction markets: evidence from Polymarket

papers.key_result: Ranking by points vs ordinal models: league-table points rankings are coarse summaries that discard margin information; ordinal paired-comparison models recover finer strength orderings and predict head-to-head outcomes better. Adaptation: replace naive points-based priors in GSE's pre-season ratings with ordinal-model strength estimates that use scoreline information.
papers.title: Ranking by points and ordinal models for paired comparisons

papers.key_result: USA Ultimate Frisbee (18-page full read): interpretable least-squares point-differential ratings beat the official USAU rating algorithm in MSE and MAD in every season/division shown (~0.25-point MAD gain), with comparable ranking violations. Adaptation: use LS point-differential ratings as GSE's transparent baseline layer beneath the black-box models — cheap, interpretable, and empirically superior to the incumbent official system.
papers.title: An Empirical Study of Least Squares Ratings for USA Ultimate Frisbee

papers.key_result: G-Elo: discretize margin of victory into outcome categories and fit Elo on the multinomial. NFL: 7-category frequency-estimated G-Elo — log score 0.6224, RPS 0.2166, accuracy 0.6656 — beats Elo-Davidson (0.6304 / 0.2200 / 0.6375). Adaptation: GSE's Elo core should be G-Elo with MOV categories tuned per sport; frequency estimation beats parametric Davidson for NFL score distributions.
papers.title: G-Elo: Generalization of the Elo algorithm by modeling the discretized Margin of Victory

papers.key_result: Least squares for cardinal paired comparisons (69 pages): full graph-Laplacian treatment of margin-based LS ratings — Var(mu_hat)=sigma^2 N^+, connectivity diagnostics, graph-correct hypothesis tests, and an omitted-covariate gate. Adaptation: GSE's margin-based ratings get exact uncertainty quantification via the Laplacian pseudoinverse plus a connectivity check that flags weeks where the matchup graph is too sparse to trust ratings.
papers.title: Least squares for cardinal paired comparisons data

papers.key_result: Tractable ridge regression for paired comparisons: penalized likelihood l_lambda(mu)=l(mu)-(lambda/2)sum mu_i^2 with no-refit PEB penalty selection. Simulations: 120 scenarios x 1000 replications — PEB uniformly best, visually indistinguishable from CV ridge. EPL: 28 seasons, 10,640 matches — PEB usually beat BRMLE, especially after 10-15 weeks. Adaptation: replace GSE's early-season MLE ratings with PEB ridge BT — finite estimates from week 1 with automatic, refit-free penalty tuning.
papers.title: Tractable Ridge Regression for Paired Comparisons

papers.key_result: Covariate Bradley-Terry with growing n (58 pages): P(i beats j)=exp(b_i-b_j+Z_ijk^T gamma)/(1+exp(...)). Core finding (Fig. 1): omitting a real covariate makes merit-estimation error NOT shrink with n — permanent bias. NBA 2018-19 (30 teams, 1230 games): home effect gamma_hat=0.45, SE 0.065, p=2.1e-12. Incidental-parameter bias in gamma has closed-form correction gamma_hat_bc. Adaptation: GSE's rating likelihood becomes covariate-BT (home, rest, travel, QB status) with bias-corrected global coefficients.
papers.title: Inference in a generalized Bradley-Terry model for paired comparisons with covariates and a growing number of subjects

papers.key_result: Strength-dependent ties and order effects: tie probability and the white/home advantage grow with the average strength of the pair. US Chess Open 2006-2019 (24,888 games): full model DIC 43,821 vs David-1988 44,658; beta_1=0.120 (0.103, 0.138) — draw probability 0.238 for evenly matched average players vs 0.489 for evenly matched strong players; white win-to-loss odds 1.20 -> 1.244 with strength. Adaptation: GSE's draw lanes get strength-dependent tie mass; test HFA x team-quality interaction in the ATS model.
papers.title: Paired comparison models with strength-dependent ties and order effects

papers.key_result: Cyclicality/intransitivity in paired comparisons (49 pages + supplement): Hodge decomposition nu = nu_linear + nu_cyclic; FTBS sparse cyclic-triad selection recovers structure with M\SE 0.72 (~oracle 0.69) vs full model 6.35 and reduced transitive model 6.63 (~1000% worse). EPL 2022-23: 3 cyclic triads selected (AIC 1101.39 vs 1118.56); betting illustration: mispricing from assuming transitivity yields TotalWin=19.5 units/round-robin. Adaptation: weekly cyclic lack-of-fit diagnostic on GSE data; FTBS-identified rock-paper-scissors triples as matchup intel; dominance-score fallback ranking.
papers.title: Modeling cyclicality and intransitivity in paired comparisons data
